question: Does an image-based check (page image plus rescued text, one fidelity question) route rf06 and rf07 to OCR without newly routing any document labelled usable?
decision: PASS opens a separate change and ADR that confirm the check on new documents before any default moves. FAIL is recorded and issue #161 stays open.

hypotheses.statement: With the local Clef-Flash Q8_0 image arm at its D2 threshold, rf06 and rf07 both route to OCR under the 10% rule, and no document labelled usable is newly routed.
hypotheses.null: rf06 or rf07 does not route, or at least one usable document is newly routed.

decision_rule: PASS when the local image arm meets both pass-rule parts on the primary population (pass_rule below). FAIL otherwise. The hosted Jev arm is a required control: without its scores the report gives no verdict. The control does not change the verdict; the outcome table states what each combination means.

word_check.definition: Experiment 38 candidate A, unchanged: min(real-word ratio, script consistency)
word_check.scores: committed Experiment 38 output/candidate_a.json, LiteParse tier, reused page by page only where the page text SHA-256 equals the text extracted here
word_check.limit: candidate A needs wordfreq, which is not installed and cannot be fetched without a download. Its scores exist only on the Experiment 38 classified pages (junk and healthy), so this arm is reported on the classified population only.

clef_image.request_shape: {model, state: {text: <text head>}, images: [<base64 PNG>], questions: {fidelity: {type: noul, instructions: <question>}}}; the exact image encoding the server accepts is recorded by the smoke test

jev_image.model_id_rule: record the returned model id for every page; stop the run if it differs from the first one recorded

request.question: Does the text match the text written or printed on the page image?
request.text_head_rule: the first 2,000 characters (Python code points) of the LiteParse page text after the shipped normaliser; no other cleaning
request.never_asked: readability or naturalness of the text

render.rule: render each page with poppler pdftoppm at 150 DPI; if the long side is above 1,568 px, scale down to 1,568 px with Lanczos and keep the aspect ratio. A page with a side under 280 px stops the run.
render.reuse_check: the Experiment 33 renders (output/.pages) are not reused: they are not 150 DPI and their long side is 1,600 px
render.storage: gitignored output/.renders/; only SHA-256 values are committed

source_data.precondition: Experiment 33 freeze.py --check prints 'freeze verified', run in a checkout that holds its corpus
source_data.text_under_test: LiteParse adapter page text, OCR off, shipped normaliser (the text the rescue chain returns today); pypdf text is extracted and hash-checked but not scored
source_data.text_identity_check: every LiteParse and pypdf page text SHA-256 must equal the committed Experiment 38 output/rescue_text.json row; any difference stops the run
source_data.classes: page classes (junk, healthy, grey, excluded) are taken unchanged from Experiment 38 output/rescue_text.json, LiteParse tier
source_data.rescued_documents: documents whose Experiment 33 sampled_baseline routing row has extraction_fallback_backend = liteparse: tl04 tl05 tl06 tl07 tl08 rf01 rf02 rf03 rf04 rf05 rf06 rf07 rf08 (263 pages)
source_data.prior_routes: Experiment 33 output/arm_sampled_baseline/routing.json ocr_required; a prior route is kept in every arm

populations.fit: healthy LiteParse pages of the 38 documents that are not rf06 or rf07: 561 pages
populations.scored: every LiteParse page with non-empty text after strip. A page with empty text is not scored and never flags.
populations.primary_routing: all scored pages of the rescued documents (what production would see)
populations.classified_routing: only junk and healthy pages of the rescued documents; used to compare all four arms, because the word check has scores only there
populations.page_level: junk pages (89, of which 54 in rf06 and rf07) and healthy pages (565) of all 40 documents

order: 1. Score the 561 fit pages with the local arm (phase fit).
2. Fit the local threshold (D2) and commit it to plan.json through an amendment.
3. Score every other scored page with the local arm (phase rest).
4. Repeat 1 to 3 with the hosted arm after the approval in decision_register.
No rf06 or rf07 page and no junk page is scored by an arm before that arm's threshold is committed.

threshold_rule.name: Experiment 38 equal-cost rule
threshold_rule.definition: sort the fit-page P(yes) values; allowance = floor(0.02 x fit pages); threshold = the value at index allowance; a page flags when P(yes) < threshold
threshold_rule.fitted_on: the fit population only, per arm
threshold_rule.limit: the fit documents are the test documents. The result shows whether the idea works; it does not show that it generalises.

routing_rules.ten_percent: a document routes when it routed before (prior route) or when its flagged pages reach 10% of its page count (the current production fraction; Experiment 38 routing_simulation)
routing_rules.one_page: a document routes when it routed before or when at least one of its pages flags
routing_rules.flags_count_only_on: pages of rescued documents (the check only sees rescued text)

pass_rule.part_1: rf06 and rf07 both route under the 10% rule
pass_rule.part_2: no document labelled usable in Experiment 33 labels.json is newly routed (routed now, not routed before) under the 10% rule
pass_rule.population: primary_routing for the image arms; classified_routing for the word check
pass_rule.one_page_rule: reported for every arm; it does not decide

outcome_table.local PASS, hosted FAIL: PASS for the local arm. The report names the documents where the arms differ.

ocr_cost.seconds_estimate: pages x 38.2 s (dots.mocr seconds per page, Experiment 38 false_positive_cost)

runtime_checks: R1: llama-server --version and GET /props report build 11941.
R2: verify_llamacpp_runtime (experiments/_lib/llamacpp_runtime.py) checks the build and the SHA-256 of Clef-Flash-Q8_0.gguf against runtime.models.
R3: the runner hashes mmproj-Clef-Flash-Q8_0.gguf against frozen and confirms the server command holds --mmproj with that file.
R4: smoke test on bd01 page 2 (healthy, CC BY): its own text (right) and the text of bd02 page 2 (wrong). P(yes | right) must exceed P(yes | wrong) by at least 0.2.
R5: a server started with --no-mmproj must reject the image request, and the runner must stop before any score.
R6: the server listens on 127.0.0.1 only.
stopping_rules: Stop before any score if R1 to R6 fails.
Stop if any extracted page text differs from Experiment 38, or if Experiment 33 freeze.py --check fails.
Stop the local arm if the 40-page speed estimate for all scored pages exceeds 6 hours.
Stop the hosted arm if the 5-page cost estimate for all scored pages exceeds USD 10 (price USD 42 per billion input tokens).
Stop the hosted arm on HTTP 401, 403 or a rejected image, or when the returned model id changes.
Stop if free memory falls under 15%.
If more than 10 pages of an arm fail after 2 retries each, stop; the result is INCONCLUSIVE.
Score each page once per arm. A resumed run keeps earlier scores and never rescores.
